citations.claim: body 0 vx drifts due to integration error by violating step
body 2 vx also strongly altered at violating step
total energy drifts at violating step showing integration error

counterfactual.change: Reduced dt from 0.025067668647436092 to 0.005 with all other fields identical (steps=5, same bodies/G/seed); finer integration removes high-acceleration truncation error and momentum stays conserved.

explanation: Shrunk scenario has high G=4.07 and massive fast bodies 0 and 2 that converge to 1.08 distance by step 5. Despite substep splitting (capped at 16 substeps per outer step, dt=0.025 -> effective ~1.5ms), the leapfrog integration error accumulates strongly during the close, high-acceleration encounter (potential deepens from -90 to -210). Momentum drifts: momentum_x changes from -155.15 at step 0 to -154.85 at step 5 and momentum_y from 24.84 to 25.08, angular momentum and energy also drift, with momentum change 0.385 exceeding allowed 0.194 at step 5. Reducing only dt to 0.005 (same steps, G, masses, positions) eliminates the violation, confirming coarse time resolution vs strong forces is the cause.
vision_note: Steps 2 to 5 show a tight pair of bodies in the upper-left remaining at very close separation with only short dotted trails, while a third isolated body sits far in the lower-right and barely moves. No visible explosion, tunneling, or boundary collision occurs; the only event is the sustained close encounter of the upper pair.
